title: The Way Things Are Now

beats.what: Boyd physically restrains Jim from opening the door to the creatures mimicking familiar voices
Donna refuses to open Colony House despite cries outside; Kenny and residents are still running
A creature stops in front of a car and stands perfectly still before killing Boyd's sister
Boyd explains the talisman rule to Jim for the first time: doors and windows shut, creatures cannot enter
Fatima tells Julie to cover windows so the creatures cannot trick her if she cannot see them
Boyd's sister story delivered: she got out of the car and was skinned alive while he froze and hid
Jim presses Boyd on what happens if they get in; Boyd says a gun is useless
Ethan's leg fragment extracted in the RV under Boyd and Kristi's care

character_beats.beat: Wants to protect Colony House yet her refusal to open the door nearly kills Boyd and the newcomers; she enforces the rule but it is visibly costing her
Wants to lead Jim through the first night with calm authority yet his sister story reveals he survived by abandoning her; his authority rests on a foundation of survivor guilt
Wants action and escape yet is forced into stillness and trust by a man he does not know

key_lines.line: They are not people and they are not here to help, Jim!
key_lines.why: First hard statement of the creatures' nature; opens the season's core ontological question

key_lines.line: They'd ripped her face off, right in front of me, ripped it clean off.
key_lines.why: The show's most visceral backstory beat; establishes what the creatures actually do

key_lines.line: It's been three years, six months and 17 days, and I can still hear my sister screaming.
key_lines.why: Boyd's precise countdown reveals how long people can be trapped; makes the horror mathematical

key_lines.line: Even a nightmare can look like a dream.
key_lines.why: Fatima's rooftop frame for the place; inverted dread as a survival philosophy

open_loops: Who or what is Victor, and how long has he actually been in the town?
What happened to Boyd's wife, referenced obliquely through guilt?
Why does Donna count days so precisely?
What do the creatures want beyond hunting?
Why did two cars arrive simultaneously, which Victor says has never happened before?

payoffs.what: Boyd's warning that the creatures mimic voices is demonstrated when they imitate familiar cries outside the Colony House door

contradiction.wants: To lead the newcomers through the night safely and prove the system works
contradiction.does: Cannot answer Jim's basic question of why a gun is useless, exposing that the system is survived, not understood

tone_notes: Two silences bracket the episode's emotional center: 91 seconds (02:44-04:15) holding on the title card and song, and 69 seconds (46:24-47:33) near the close. The opening eight minutes hit density spikes of 149-195 words/min, the highest sustained intensity in the batch, matching the sprint to Colony House. Minutes 23-24 drop to 20-45 w/min as Boyd tells the sister story; the camera and script both slow to let the horror of stillness land.
